title: introduce-coreset-traffic-slicing-for-targeted-canary-evals
author: Sophie Park
release_notes: Introduce traffic coreset sampler and slice stability guard for more efficient, targeted canary evaluation; enables shorter canary windows and lower cost while preserving signal fidelity.
description:
Motivation: Running full-traffic canaries for every rollout is costly and slow. For a subset of rollouts (model minor bumps, scheduler tweaks) we want a small, representative traffic 'coreset' that preserves signal for latency/throughput/SLO regressions while reducing test volume and compute cost. This PR implements a traffic coreset sampler plus a slice-stability rollout guard that protects against selection drift and ensures the coreset remains predictive over time.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) coreset_sampler: a lightweight stratified weighted sampler that maintains a bounded-size sample while preserving distribution over key axes (tenant, endpoint, request size, model variant). 2) impact-weighting: requests are weighted by estimated per-request resource cost so the coreset prioritizes high-cost/high-impact traffic slices. 3) slice-stability-guard: a canary guard that computes divergence metrics (Wasserstein distance on request-size, KL on endpoint distribution, p95 delta on latency) between historical reference traffic and live slice; when divergence > threshold it pauses or expands the slice. 4) dashboard and alerting tiles for slice fidelity and slice drift. 5) e2e harness and deterministic replay tests for reproducibility.

Config knobs: sample_size (default 10k requests/min), stratify_keys (default [tenant, endpoint, prompt_len_bucket]), impact_weight_alpha (0.7 default), stability_thresholds (per-metric tunables), auto_expand_on_drift (boolean, default false).

Rollout plan: staged rollout: dev->staging (2 days) with synthetic replay -> canary ring (5% traffic) using coreset slice -> gradual enable across rings with automated monitoring gating. We ran a controlled live traffic dry-run on staging that shows the coreset preserved p90/p99 deltas within 3% of full-traffic canary for a 12.5% sample.

Backward compatibility: No user-facing API changes. Canary controller gains optional flags to enable coreset-based evaluation. Default behavior remains full-traffic canaries until enabled via config.

Related work: complements the existing canary detectors (percentile-decay and correlation canary) by reducing the evaluation surface; references: ENG-10234, perf-canary PRs for percentile-decay.

Limitations: coreset effectiveness depends on good stratification keys; large distributional shifts where unseen endpoints appear require guard intervention. This PR intentionally runs slice-stability checks and defaults to fail-open (pause canary) until manual review if severe drift is detected.

review_comments: Marcus Varela (reviewer): The sampler looks sound but can we add a deterministic seed and a way to snapshot the coreset for postmortem replays?
Author (Sophie Park): Added deterministic seeding and snapshot API in the latest commit; updated tests to cover replay equality.

Anita Kumar (reviewer): The stability thresholds are conservative; recommend per-tenant overrides and a metric for resource-cost drift. Also, please ensure the guard prefers auto-expansion before pause for low-severity drift.

Author (Sophie Park): Added per-tenant threshold map and included resource-cost p95 delta as a metric. Default behavior changed to auto-expand by 2x on low-severity drift and pause only on high-severity drift (>2x thresholds).
Diego Salazar (reviewer): CI integration spike: the perf-e2e flaked once in staging but rerun passed. Can you add a retry stanza in the pipeline?
Author (Sophie Park): Added a single-retry to the e2e job and a short jitter to prevent thundering replays.
ci_checks: perf-e2e: fail on first run (transient replay ordering) -> rerun: pass
merge_details: Merged via squash by Marcus Varela on 2026-03-03. Merge commit: abcdef1234567890. Merge method: squash. Merged_at: 2026-03-03.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: slice may miss rare but critical request types leading to false negatives in canary detection. Mitigations: 1) stability guard monitors distributional drift and pauses/expands slice; 2) per-tenant override to include user-provided critical endpoints; 3) fallback to full-traffic canary on manual inspection or if slice fails validation.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for sampling invariants (stratification, weighting). Replay harness deterministic: 10 runs identical across CI nodes. Staging dry-run: compared full-traffic vs coreset canary across 7 model variants and 3 endpoints; p90/p99 deltas within 3% for samples >= 10k/min. Live canary (5% ring, synthetic traffic): no regressions observed; slice drift alert fired once due to synthetic skew and auto-expanded slice to remediate. Post-merge: enabled in staging for 48h with monitoring alerts configured.
notes_for_ops: Operational dashboard tiles added: coreset_fidelity_{p90,p99}, slice_wasserstein, slice_kl_endpoint, estimated_cost_savings. Runbook located at docs/perf-canary/coreset.md with rollback steps. To disable coreset mode set canary.controller.use_coreset=false in config.
